reason: The text fragment does not support the statement that only priests can offer sacrifice to Yahweh. The passage describes God commissioning Moses to gather the elders (זִקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) of Israel and tells them they will go into the wilderness to sacrifice (וְנִזְבְּחָ֖ה) to Yahweh. This narrative context (Exodus 3-4) predates the formal establishment of the priesthood at Sinai. The text explicitly mentions non-priestly figures—the elders and people—participating in sacrifice to Yahweh without any restriction or indication that only priests can perform this act. The passage contains no language suggesting a priestly monopoly on sacrifice.
